newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai king appoints new cabinet led by Chavalit.
newsitem.headline: Thai king appoints new cabinet led by Chavalit.

text.p: Thai King Bhumibol Adulyadej on Friday appointed a new 49-member cabinet proposed by Prime Minister-designate Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, and the government is due to be sworn in on December 1.
Visanu Krua-ngam, secretary-general of the cabinet, said the cabinet proposed by Chavalit would begin work the day after it was sworn into office.

"They will all be sworn in on December 1," Visanu said in a televised address to announce the cabinet. "Then they can officially assume their positions and hold the first cabinet meeting on December 2."

Chavalit's New Aspiration Party (NAP) won a slim two-seat victory over its rival Democrat Party in the November 17 general election and became the core of a six-party coalition that holds 221 seats in the 393-seat lower house.
Chavalit replaces Banharn Silpa-archa who dissolved parliament in September after a bruising no-confidence debate where he and his Chart Thai party were accused of mismanagement and corruption.
The NAP-led cabinet includes politicians from all six parties and the portfolios are divided up according to the number of seats won in the election.
Key cabinet members include Chavalit, who will be the country's 22nd prime minister and hold the defence portfolio, Amnuay Viravan as finance minister and Narongchai Akrasanee as commerce minister.

Amnuay, a respected economist and former finance minister, will also be deputy premier. He and Naronghai, chairman of Thailand's General Finance and Securities Plc, will be two of the unelected experts appointed under the NAP quota trying to revive Thailand's economy.
The second largest coalition member, the Chart Pattana Party (CPP), will have a role in industry and foreign trade.
The charismatic but ageing CPP leader, former prime minister Chatichai Choonhavan, will play an advisory role in economic and foreign relations, coalition sources said.
CPP deputy leader Korn Dabbaransi will be deputy prime minister and industry minister and Prachuab Chaiyasarn, also deputy CPP leader, will be foreign minister, Visanu said.
Chavalit, a former army chief, will supervise security issues and NAP secretary general Snoh Thienthong was named as interior minister.
The Ministry of the Interior deals with social welfare issues, overseeing a police force of more than 200,000 and supervising elections.

The announcement of the cabinet comes after wrangling among the coalition partners over how to share the various ministries. Most of the delay was caused by differences between the NAP and CPP over how to divide the economic ministries.
Chavalit has said his government will give top priority to boosting Thailand's economy.

The smaller parties in the coalition -- Social Action, Prachakorn Thai, Seritham and Moun Chon -- were assigned the ministries dealing with social welfare, public health, science and technology and the environment.
Prachakorn Thai has been handed the tough task of solving Bangkok's notorious traffic congestion, coalition sources said.
